speaker_concepts.verbatim_description: It shows the average price where real money actually changed hands throughout the day. VWAP is actually the institutional anchor point.
resets every session and shows you intraday institutional activity.
captures the bigger swing trade positioning.
reveals the major trend and where long-term players are anchored.
When VWAP intersects with a high volume node from the volume profile, you get what institutions call a confluence anchor. This is where massive institutional orders are likely sitting.
means the market is in balance. Buyers and sellers are evenly matched. Price will likely chop around this level.
means one side is winning decisively. The steeper the angle, the stronger the institutional flow.
When daily, weekly, and monthly VWAP all point in the same direction, you have institutional alignment.
When all three VWAPs are stacked bullishly, daily above weekly above monthly, and price is above all three, you have what we call institutional consensus.
VWAP anchored to major events, earnings announcements, Fed meetings, company keynotes. These create much more powerful levels than random daily resets.
shows you where the big money positioned themselves around major news.
showing you mathematical probability in real time, the statistical boundaries of normal price action.
The plus one and minus one bands contain about 68% of price action. This is the normal trading range.
When price hits these levels [plus two/minus two], you get mean reversion signals.
The plus three and minus three bands are the extreme levels. Only 0.3% of price action should reach here.
In strong trends, price will ride along the plus one or minus one band. It doesn't return to VWAP. Instead, it uses the band as dynamic support or resistance.
shows institutional defense. They're actively protecting that level.
shows uncertainty.
a strong close through VWAP with volume, that's capitulation.
Price breaks below VWAP by a few candles, triggers all the stops, then immediately reverses back above. This isn't random. It's institutions grabbing liquidity before the real move higher.
Bull market, price stays above yearly VWAP for months, even during corrections. Bear market, yearly VWAP becomes impenetrable resistance that caps every rally.
The quarterly VWAP strategy is pure gold during earning season. Institutions position their portfolios around quarterly performance.
When daily says buy, but weekly says sell, weekly wins. When weekly says buy, but monthly says sell, monthly wins. The longer time frame always has more institutional commitment behind it.
When all time frames align, daily, weekly, monthly, and yearly VWAP all broken in the same direction, you're witnessing institutional herding.
During these dead zones, price can drift through VWAP with zero resistance because no institutions are participating.
